back: A subroutine that calls itself with a smaller version of the problem until a case is reached that is answered directly.
The case answered without a recursive call; it stops the recursion.
The case that calls the subroutine again with an argument closer to the base case.
Memory holding a frame (return address, parameters, local variables) for each active subroutine call.
Once the base case returns, each call completes in reverse order and passes its value to the call that made it.
The calls never stop and the stack overflows (RecursionError in Python).
Statements before the recursive call run in call order; statements after it run in reverse order.
Recursion: clear for trees and divide and conquer, but uses stack memory and is slower. Iteration: fixed memory and usually faster.
Each call pushes a frame and jumps to the subroutine; each return pops the frame and jumps back.
